page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.medium is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by a single dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 physical core. Operating at 2.6 GHz, this instance features 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks reflect its single-core architecture. The server achieves average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1516.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1500.0. However, multi-core and multi-threaded benchmarks, such as the stress-ng multi-core test (1516.59) and Geekbench multi-core test (1502.0), fall into the lower performance tiers due to the single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth is measured at 96.93 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 31.16 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

The instance is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c7gn.medium offers a low-entry hardware profile for ARM64 development, providing dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of multi-threading. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded workloads, basic network-optimized tasks, utility scripting, software compilation testing, and low-traffic web serving where high network throughput relative to compute size is required.
